cards.back: Traverse RIGHT to LEFT, carrying a running max (maxSoFar). At each index: (1) write maxSoFar, (2) then update maxSoFar = max(maxSoFar, current value). O(n) time, O(1) space. Key: write BEFORE updating, so maxSoFar means 'biggest strictly to the right.' Generalizes to: any question about 'everything to one side' → traverse from that side with a running aggregate.
cards.front: Array problem asks for the 'greatest element to the right' of each position. What's the pattern?

cards.back: Because maxSoFar must represent the max strictly to the RIGHT of the current index, not including the current element itself. If you update first, you'd be counting the current element as its own 'greatest to the right' — wrong. Order: write, then update.
cards.front: In Replace Elements with Greatest on Right, why must you write maxSoFar BEFORE updating it?

cards.back: Product of Array Except Self (running products from both sides) and Trapping Rain Water (running maxes from both sides). Same family: suffix/prefix aggregates computed in one pass by traversing from the side you're aggregating.
cards.front: Name two other problems that use the 'reverse traversal + running aggregate' trick.
